questions.q: In 'The Goatherd and the Goat', why did the Goat stray away from the flock?
choices: It was tempted by a patch of clover
It was chased away by a hungry wolf
It wanted to find water to drink
It was looking for its lost mother
questions.evidence: tempted by a patch of clover

questions.q: In 'The Goatherd and the Goat', what did the Goatherd beg the Goat to do after breaking its horn?
choices: Not tell the master
Run back to the flock
Forgive him at once
Hide in the barn

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'The Goatherd and the Goat'?
choices: Wicked deeds will not stay hid
Always stay close to the flock
Clover is bad for goats to eat
Masters should be kind to goats
questions.evidence: Wicked deeds will not stay hid.

questions.q: In 'The Miser', how did the Thief find out where the gold was?
choices: He saw the Miser make so many trips to the spot
The Miser told him about the gold by mistake
He found an old map that showed where it was buried
A passerby on the road told him about the gold
questions.evidence: He made so many trips that a Thief, who had been observing him

questions.q: In 'The Miser', why did the stranger say a stone was worth as much as the lost gold?
choices: The Miser never used the gold, so it did him no good
The stone was really made of gold under the dirt
Stones from that garden are worth a lot of money
The stone would scare off any other thieves later
questions.evidence: A possession is worth no more than the use we make of it.

questions.q: In 'The Wolf and the House Dog', what did the Wolf notice on the Dog's neck?
choices: The hair was worn and the skin was chafed
A shiny gold tag with the master's name on it
A big scar left from a fight with a wolf
A pretty red ribbon tied in a bow
questions.evidence: the hair on the Dog's neck was worn and the skin was chafed

questions.q: In 'The Wolf and the House Dog', why did the Wolf run back to the woods?
choices: He would rather be free than fed and chained
He was afraid of the people with canes
He did not like the cake the Dog described
The Dog turned on him and chased him away
questions.evidence: There is nothing worth so much as liberty.

questions.q: In 'The Fox and the Hedgehog', why did the Fox not want the flies driven away?
choices: Full flies would just be replaced by hungry ones
He liked the flies and wanted them to stay
He wanted to save the flies to eat later
He did not trust the Hedgehog's long sharp quills
